sources.cite: J. K. Reinker and P. B. Mason, Steam Turbines for Large Power Applications, GE Power Systems GER-3646D: pp. 9-11 stages, balance piston, inner shells and their joint flanges; p. 13 diaphragms in the inner shell, shells on the bearing standards; p. 15 coupling bolts and joint studs

M. Boss, Steam Turbines for STAG Combined-Cycle Power Systems, GE Power Systems GER-3582E (1996): p. 12 the thrust bearing in the front standard, near the HP stages; pp. 16-17 combined stop and control valves piped to the lower casing; pp. 20-21 joint flanges and packings

IMIA working group paper WGP 42 (05), Maintenance and Overhaul of Steam Turbines (2005): 2.A.2 rotors and their flange couplings; tables 8-9 overhaul tasks (the upper casings removed, bearings opened, coupling bolts checked)
US Navy, Fireman, NAVEDTRA 14104 (1992), chapter 5 Steam Turbines: casings, rotors, radial and thrust bearings, labyrinth shaft packing glands

US NRC, Westinghouse Technology Systems Manual, section 7.3 Main Turbine, MSR and EHC (a course copy): 7.3.2.1 steam chests with stop and governor valves each side, 7.3.2.2 rotors forged, flanged rigid couplings

S. Rameshkumar, Turbine overhauling procedure (after the Siemens/KWU service manual, 2006): pp. 2-11 the take-apart order (insulation, bearing pedestal tops and thrust bearing, uncoupling, outer casing, blade carrier and inner casing, glands, rotor, lower halves); pp. 52-60 reassembly
US patent 5,257,905 (Westinghouse, 1993): flanges formed at the end of each rotor, joined by coupling bolts and nuts
US patent 5,511,941 (1996), background: the shell bolts loosened before the upper half shell is lifted

lagging_upper.name: Lagging, upper half
lagging_upper.does: Insulation and its sheet-metal cladding over the upper casing: keeps the heat in and the outside safe to touch. The first thing off in an overhaul.

lagging_lower.name: Lagging, lower half
lagging_lower.does: Insulation and cladding round the lower casing.

casing_lower.name: Outer casing, lower half
casing_lower.does: Holds the steam; rests on the bearing pedestals and carries the inner casing. Its flanges meet the upper half at the horizontal joint.

casing_upper.name: Outer casing, upper half
casing_upper.does: Bolted to the lower half at the horizontal joint; lifted off to open the turbine.

inner_lower.name: Inner casing, lower half
inner_lower.does: A second shell inside the outer one: takes the inlet steam's full pressure and carries the blade carriers.

inner_upper.name: Inner casing, upper half
inner_upper.does: Bolted to the lower half through its own joint flanges.

carrier_lower.name: Blade carrier, lower half
carrier_lower.does: Holds the lower halves of the stationary blade rows in the inner casing.
carrier_lower.sealed_why: The stationary blades are fixed in the carrier's grooves: in an overhaul the carrier comes out with them, and they are renewed only in a shop.

carrier_upper.name: Blade carrier, upper half
carrier_upper.does: Holds the upper halves of the stationary blade rows.
carrier_upper.sealed_why: The stationary blades are fixed in the carrier's grooves: in an overhaul the carrier comes out with them, and they are renewed only in a shop.

glands_lower.name: Shaft glands, lower halves
glands_lower.does: Labyrinth seals where the shaft leaves the casing at each end: they keep steam in and air out.

glands_upper.name: Shaft glands, upper halves
glands_upper.does: The upper halves of the labyrinth seals at both ends.

rotor.name: Rotor
rotor.does: Forged in one piece with its blade rows, balance piston, thrust collar and coupling flange; turns in the journal bearings and drives the next rotor along the shaft line.
rotor.sealed_why: The rotor is lifted out and set back as one piece: its blades are renewed only in a shop, and the rotor balanced again.

collar.name: Thrust collar
collar.does: A disc on the rotor between the thrust bearing's pads: it holds the rotor in place along its axis against the steam's push (simplified).

pedestal_f.name: Front bearing pedestal
pedestal_f.does: Stands on the foundation and carries the front journal bearing and the thrust bearing; the casing rests on it.

cap_f.name: Front pedestal cover
cap_f.does: Closes the front pedestal over its bearings; lifted off first to reach them.

brg_f_lower.name: Front journal bearing, lower half
brg_f_lower.does: Carries the rotor's weight on an oil film.

brg_f_upper.name: Front journal bearing, upper half
brg_f_upper.does: Closes the bearing over the journal.

thrust.name: Thrust bearing
thrust.does: Pads on both faces of the thrust collar keep the rotor in its place along the axis (simplified).

pedestal_r.name: Rear bearing pedestal
pedestal_r.does: Carries the rear journal bearing; the casing's rear end rests on it.

cap_r.name: Rear pedestal cover
cap_r.does: Closes the rear pedestal over its bearing.

brg_r_lower.name: Rear journal bearing, lower half
brg_r_lower.does: Carries the rotor's weight on an oil film.

brg_r_upper.name: Rear journal bearing, upper half
brg_r_upper.does: Closes the bearing over the journal.

valve_l.name: Stop and control valve, left
valve_l.does: The combined valve chest on this side of the casing: live steam passes its stop valve, then its control valve, into the casing.
valve_l.material: Cast alloy steel body under lagging

stop_l.name: Stop valve disc, left
stop_l.does: Shuts off the steam at once when the turbine trips.

ctrl_l.name: Control valve plug, left
ctrl_l.does: Opens as far as the governor asks: it sets how much steam goes to the blades.

servo_l.name: Valve actuator, left
servo_l.does: The hydraulic servomotor that moves the valve: oil pressure opens it, a spring closes it.

valve_r.name: Stop and control valve, right
valve_r.does: The combined valve chest on this side of the casing: live steam passes its stop valve, then its control valve, into the casing.
valve_r.material: Cast alloy steel body under lagging

stop_r.name: Stop valve disc, right
stop_r.does: Shuts off the steam at once when the turbine trips.

ctrl_r.name: Control valve plug, right
ctrl_r.does: Opens as far as the governor asks: it sets how much steam goes to the blades.

servo_r.name: Valve actuator, right
servo_r.does: The hydraulic servomotor that moves the valve: oil pressure opens it, a spring closes it.

srow_u1.name: Stage 1 stationary blades, upper
srow_u1.does: The first stage's fixed blades: they speed the steam up and turn it onto the moving blades.

srow_l1.name: Stage 1 stationary blades, lower
srow_l1.does: The lower half of the first stage's fixed blades.

mrow_1.name: Stage 1 moving blades
mrow_1.does: The first stage's blades on the rotor: the steam pushes them round. They lengthen stage by stage as the steam expands.

text: Set the front bearing pedestal on the foundation.
Set the rear bearing pedestal on the foundation.
Lower the outer casing's lower half onto the pedestals and line it up with the shaft line.
needs: pedestal_f
The casing rests on the front pedestal: set it first.
Lift the lower casing off before the front pedestal is moved.
pedestal_r
The casing rests on the rear pedestal: set it first.
Lift the lower casing off before the rear pedestal is moved.

text: Set the left stop and control valve beside the casing and connect it to the lower half.
needs: casing_lower
The valve's steam lead goes into the lower casing: set the casing first.
Disconnect the valve before the lower casing is lifted.

text: Fit the left stop valve disc and its stem in the chest.
needs: valve_l
The disc goes inside the valve chest: set the chest first.
Take the stop valve disc out before the chest is moved.

text: Fit the left control valve plug and its stem in the chest.
needs: valve_l
The plug goes inside the valve chest: set the chest first.
Take the control valve plug out before the chest is moved.

text: Mount the left valve actuator on the chest and couple it to the stems.
needs: stop_l
Fit the stop valve disc before the actuator closes the chest.
Take the actuator off before the stop valve disc.
ctrl_l
Fit the control valve plug before the actuator closes the chest.
Take the actuator off before the control valve plug.

text: Set the right stop and control valve beside the casing and connect it to the lower half.
needs: casing_lower
The valve's steam lead goes into the lower casing: set the casing first.
Disconnect the valve before the lower casing is lifted.

text: Fit the right stop valve disc and its stem in the chest.
needs: valve_r
The disc goes inside the valve chest: set the chest first.
Take the stop valve disc out before the chest is moved.

text: Fit the right control valve plug and its stem in the chest.
needs: valve_r
The plug goes inside the valve chest: set the chest first.
Take the control valve plug out before the chest is moved.

text: Mount the right valve actuator on the chest and couple it to the stems.
needs: stop_r
Fit the stop valve disc before the actuator closes the chest.
Take the actuator off before the stop valve disc.
ctrl_r
Fit the control valve plug before the actuator closes the chest.
Take the actuator off before the control valve plug.

text: Lower the inner casing's lower half into the outer casing.
needs: casing_lower
The inner casing sits in the outer casing's lower half: set that first.
Lift the lower inner casing out before the outer casing's lower half is moved.

text: Lower the blade carrier's lower half into the inner casing.
needs: inner_lower
The blade carrier sits in the inner casing: set the lower inner casing first.
Lift the lower blade carrier out before the lower inner casing.

text: Stage 1's lower stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 2's lower stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 3's lower stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 4's lower stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 5's lower stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 6's lower stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 7's lower stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 8's lower stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Fit the lower halves of the shaft glands at both ends of the casing.
needs: casing_lower
The glands sit in the lower casing's ends: set the casing first.
Take the lower glands out before the lower casing is lifted.

text: Roll the front journal bearing's lower half into the front pedestal.
needs: pedestal_f
The bearing sits in the front pedestal: set the pedestal first.
Roll the lower front bearing out before the pedestal is moved.

text: Roll the rear journal bearing's lower half into the rear pedestal.
needs: pedestal_r
The bearing sits in the rear pedestal: set the pedestal first.
Roll the lower rear bearing out before the pedestal is moved.

text: Lower the rotor level onto the lower journal bearings, clear of the blades and glands.
why: A rotor set down off level or touched against the blades bends blades and scores seals.
needs: brg_f_lower
The rotor rests on the journal bearings: roll the lower front bearing in first.
Lift the rotor out before the lower front bearing comes out.
brg_r_lower
The rotor rests on the journal bearings: roll the lower rear bearing in first.
Lift the rotor out before the lower rear bearing comes out.
carrier_lower
Set the lower blade carrier before the rotor: it cannot go in under the blades.
Lift the rotor out before the lower blade carrier.
glands_lower
Fit the lower glands before the rotor: they go in under the shaft.
Lift the rotor out before the lower glands.

text: Stage 1's moving blades come with the rotor.
Stage 2's moving blades come with the rotor.
Stage 3's moving blades come with the rotor.
Stage 4's moving blades come with the rotor.
Stage 5's moving blades come with the rotor.
Stage 6's moving blades come with the rotor.
Stage 7's moving blades come with the rotor.
Stage 8's moving blades come with the rotor.
The thrust collar is part of the rotor.
Close the front journal bearing with its upper half.
needs: rotor
The upper half closes over the rotor's journal: set the rotor first.
Take the upper front bearing off before the rotor is lifted.

text: Close the rear journal bearing with its upper half.
needs: rotor
The upper half closes over the rotor's journal: set the rotor first.
Take the upper rear bearing off before the rotor is lifted.

text: Fit the upper halves of the shaft glands over the shaft.
needs: rotor
The upper glands close over the shaft: set the rotor first.
Take the upper glands off before the rotor is lifted.

text: Lower the blade carrier's upper half over the rotor onto the lower half.
needs: rotor
The upper carrier's blades fit between the rotor's: set the rotor first.
Lift the upper blade carrier off before the rotor.
carrier_lower
The upper carrier sits on the lower one: set that first.
Lift the upper blade carrier off before the lower one.

text: Stage 1's upper stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 2's upper stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 3's upper stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 4's upper stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 5's upper stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 6's upper stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 7's upper stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Stage 8's upper stationary blades come with the blade carrier.
Lower the inner casing's upper half onto the lower half.
needs: carrier_upper
The upper inner casing closes over the blade carrier: set the upper carrier first.
Lift the upper inner casing off before the upper blade carrier.
inner_lower
The upper inner casing sits on the lower one: set that first.
Lift the upper inner casing off before the lower one.

text: Fit the inner casing's joint studs and tighten their nuts.
needs: inner_upper
The studs go through both halves' flanges: set the upper inner casing first.
Take the inner casing's studs out before its upper half is lifted.

text: Lower the outer casing's upper half onto the joint on its guide pins.
why: Jacking screws take the upper half the first few millimetres off the joint, square, so it does not bind on its guide pins.
needs: inner_upper
Close the inner casing before the outer casing: set the upper inner casing first.
Lift the upper outer casing off before the upper inner casing.
inner_bolts
Tighten the inner casing's studs before the outer casing closes over them.
Lift the upper outer casing off before the inner casing's studs come out.
glands_upper
Fit the upper glands before the outer casing closes over them.
Lift the upper outer casing off before the upper glands.
casing_lower
The upper half sits on the lower half's flanges: set the lower half first.
Lift the upper outer casing off before the lower half.

text: Fit the horizontal joint's studs and tighten their nuts in the casing maker's order.
needs: casing_upper
The studs hold the two halves of the joint: set the upper casing first.
Loosen and take out all the joint's studs before the upper casing is lifted.

text: Couple the rotor to the next one: line the flanges up and fit the coupling bolts.
why: The rotors are lined up before coupling; coupled out of line they shake the bearings.
needs: rotor
The bolts join the rotor's coupling flange to the next rotor's: set the rotor first.
Take the coupling bolts out, uncoupling the rotors, before the rotor is lifted.

text: Fit the thrust bearing's pads on both faces of the thrust collar.
needs: rotor
The pads go on the faces of the rotor's thrust collar: set the rotor first.
Take the thrust bearing out before the rotor is lifted.

text: Close the front pedestal with its cover.
needs: brg_f_upper
Close the front journal bearing before the cover goes on.
Take the front pedestal's cover off before the upper front bearing.
thrust
Fit the thrust bearing before the cover goes on.
Take the front pedestal's cover off before the thrust bearing.

text: Close the rear pedestal with its cover.
needs: brg_r_upper
Close the rear journal bearing before the cover goes on.
Take the rear pedestal's cover off before the upper rear bearing.

text: Put the lower half's insulation and cladding back.
needs: casing_lower
The lagging covers the lower casing: set it first.
Strip the lower lagging before the lower casing is moved.

text: Put the upper half's insulation and cladding back, the last thing on.
needs: casing_upper
The lagging covers the upper casing: close the casing first.
Strip the upper lagging first: it covers the casing's joint and its studs.
joint_bolts
Tighten the joint's studs before they are lagged over.
Strip the upper lagging before the joint's studs are loosened.

run_exploded.why: A steam turbine runs only closed: the casing holds the steam and the bearings the rotor. Put it back together first (the lagging may stay off).
